rulings.Case Title: DELLA JOANN LOPEZ VS. MONSANTO COMPANY ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: MOTION TO ADMIT COUNSEL PRO HAC VICE
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Tuesday, August 18, 2026, Line 1, DEFENDANT MONSANTO COMPANY's MOTION TO ADMIT COUNSEL PRO HAC VICE. Defendant Monsanto Company's unopposed Motion to Admit Pro Hac Vice Counsel Joseph E. Fornadel is GRANTED. Good cause appearing, counsel Joseph E. Fornadel may appear as counsel pro hac vice for Moving Party in this action. Moving Party is ordered to prepare a proposed order which repeats the above text verbatim and email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the time set for hearing. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept302tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(302/JMQ).

rulings.Case Title: KENNETH LITTLE VS. ANTHONY PAUL CARA ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Deem Admitted Requests For Admissions, Set One Propounded On Plaintiff
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Tuesday, August 18, 2026, Line 3, DEFENDANT CONSUMER DEFENSE LAW GROUP, P.C., ANTHONY CARA, FERNANDO LEONE's Motion To Deem Admitted Requests For Admissions, Set One Propounded On Plaintiff. Defendants' unopposed Motion To Deem Admitted Requests For Admissions, Set One Propounded On Plaintiff is GRANTED. The record demonstrates Moving Defendants properly served Requests for Admission, Set One and Plaintiff Kennth Little did not provide any responses to Moving Defendants' requests. (See Code of Civil Procedure section 2033.280.) Plaintiff's failure to timely respond is not excused. No meet and confer requirement when no responses have been provided. Moving Defendants' RFAs, Set One, to Plaintiff Kennth Little are deemed admitted.
